device.model: Music Easel: Model 208 Stored Program Sound Source and Model 218 Touch Activated Voltage Source (original, 1973-74)
device.category: portable analogue performance synthesizer: complex and modulation oscillators, dual lowpass gate, control voltage sources, touch keyboard, program cards
device.based_on: Designed by Don Buchla; a consolidation of Buchla 200 series concepts in one case. Reissued from 2013 and again as the 208C/Easel Command.

sources.title: Programming and Metaprogramming in the Electro-Organism: An Operating Directive for the Music Easel (Allen Strange, Buchla and Associates, 1974)
sources.note: Tutorial rather than reference. Covers every control with numbered callouts, around 19 patch charts drawn as panel diagrams, and the program card in full (conductance table, field encodings, worked card realisations). No specification section.

sources.title: Dave Brown, ModularSynthesis.com: Buchla 208 Stored Program Sound Source (service notes on a 1973-74 unit)
sources.note: Card-by-card layout, measured oscillator ranges, scope photos, and the early timbre circuit as cross-modulation of two tracking triangle oscillators.

sources.title: Buchla Tech blog, 'The Good Thing About Standards' (2008); Sound On Sound, 'Buchla 200e: Part 1' (2005)
sources.note: Voltage standards of early 1970s 200 series modules: 0-15 V CVs, 15 V pulses, +4 dBu audio, separate connector types for each class.

sources.title: Buchla USA user guides: 218e/208 card doubler, 200e, 218e v3; Easel Command product page
sources.note: The 1.2 V/octave Buchla pitch standard; later 0-10 V CVs and 10 V/5 V pulses; 208C changes from the original.

sources.title: Synth DB, Buchla Music Easel
sources.note: Program output 1 V rms, 2 W monitor output, battery pack of about three hours, original card supply, key count.

sources.title: Gearspace review of the 2013 reissue; Perfect Circuit and Buchla product pages
sources.note: Vactrol lowpass gates, spring reverb, wavefolding timbre circuit; reissue details used only to separate later features.

architecture.synthesis_note: West Coast: a complex oscillator with harmonic addition (timbre folding and waveshape mixing), FM and AM from a modulation oscillator, and vactrol lowpass gates in place of a separate filter and VCA. No subtractive filter as such.
architecture.polyphony_mode: monophonic; the modulation oscillator can sound as a second, independent voice through Gate 2
architecture.patch_memory_note: Hardwired program cards: resistors soldered on a plug-in board replicate switch positions, slider levels and control routings.
architecture.routing: internal wiring set by switches, banana-cord patch field, and the program card
architecture.summary: Two units in one case. The 208 holds the sound sources and processors: a complex oscillator (sine mixed with spike, square or triangle, plus a timbre control that adds harmonics), a modulation oscillator that frequency or amplitude modulates it or ring modulates an external signal, a dual lowpass gate (each half a vactrol VCA, lowpass filter or both), a preamp with envelope detector, and an output section with reverb. Its control sources are a five-stage sequential voltage source, an attack-duration-decay envelope generator, a pulser (triggered ramp and trigger source), a four-output random voltage source and an inverter. Every voltage-controlled parameter has an offset slider and a processing slider for the patched voltage. The 218 is a capacitive touch keyboard giving key voltage, pressure, pulse, portamento and three preset voltages. Control voltages and pulses travel on stackable banana cords; audio stays internal apart from the preamp input and outputs. A plug-in program card, built from resistors, can replace or add to the front panel.

modules.name: Touch Activated Voltage Source (Model 218)
modules.description: Capacitive touch keyboard with no moving parts. 29 voltage keys give equal steps, held after release until another key is touched; a PRESSURE voltage follows how much finger surface is on any key; a PULSE marks each touch. A PORTAMENTO output glides linearly between key voltages at a rate set by SLOPE and a control input. Three preset plates, each with its own level knob, give a separate PRESET output, and the SHIFT selector can use them to transpose the key voltage. Every output appears on two paralleled banana jacks. Nothing reaches the 208 except by patch cord.

modules.name: Signals from Keyboard (208)
modules.description: Three banana inputs on the 208 (pulse, pressure, voltage) that bring the 218 into the sound source. VOLTAGE reaches the oscillators through their KEYBOARD switches, PULSE reaches every trigger-source selector set to 'keyboard', and PRESSURE is redistributed to the violet jacks on the patch field.

modules.name: Sequential Voltage Source
modules.description: Five stages, each with a preset output level, advanced one stage per trigger from the keyboard or the pulser (or not at all, holding the last stage). STAGES limits the cycle to three, four or five; the program card adds two. As each stage is reached it emits a pulse unless its PULSE SEQUENCE switch is down; those pulses can fire the pulser or envelope generator. Voltage on the blue jacks.

modules.name: Envelope Generator
modules.description: Attack, duration and decay, each 2 ms to 10 s. In 'transient' mode the duration slider sets the hold; in 'sustained' mode the envelope holds for as long as the trigger lasts, then decays. Triggered by the keyboard, pulser or sequencer. Output on three orange jacks.

modules.name: Pulser
modules.description: On each trigger generates a linearly falling ramp, available on the yellow jacks, and when the ramp reaches zero emits a trigger to every trigger-source selector set to 'pulser'. The ramp's length is the PERIOD, 2 ms to 10 s, voltage controlled (more voltage, shorter period). In 'self' mode its own end trigger restarts it, so it runs continuously once started.

modules.name: Random Voltage Source
modules.description: On each trigger from the keyboard or pulser (or the sequencer, from the card only), four new uncorrelated random voltages appear on the four white jacks and hold until the next trigger.

modules.name: Modulation Oscillator
modules.description: Sawtooth, square or triangle, 0.16 to 50 Hz on the panel and much higher under voltage control. Its MODULATION switch decides what it does to the sound: FM of the complex oscillator, AM of the complex oscillator, or balanced (ring) modulation of the preamp signal, all at a depth set by INDEX (0 to 1.0). It can also sound in its own right through Gate 2, and a copy of its waveform leaves on the 'mod c.v. out' jack as a control voltage.

modules.name: Balanced Modulator
modules.description: Internal multiplier, on its own card in the original, that the modulation oscillator uses for AM of the complex oscillator and for balanced modulation of the preamp signal. Index 1.0 gives full ring modulation: the carrier is suppressed and only sidebands remain.

properties.source: card 5 in Dave Brown's service notes

modules.name: Complex Oscillator
modules.description: The main sound source. PITCH covers 55 to 1760 Hz (five octaves, calibrated in octaves and half octaves) with a fine tuning knob of half an octave. A WAVESHAPE knob mixes a sine with the waveform chosen on the WAVESHAPE selector: spike, square or triangle. TIMBRE adds and accentuates harmonics (the opposite of filtering) and acts only on the sine and triangle, so it does nothing with the knob fully at spike or square. A KEYBOARD switch connects the key voltage directly; the SIGN switch sets whether a patched pitch voltage raises or lowers the pitch. Always feeds Gate 1.

properties.timbre_circuit: early 208: a second triangle oscillator tracks the first and is cross-modulated by it as timbre rises (Dave Brown)

modules.name: Inverter
modules.description: Turns a control voltage upside down on the 0 to 10 scale: 10 becomes 0, 9 becomes 1, 6 becomes 4. Rising envelopes become falling ones.

modules.name: Preamp
modules.description: External signal in on a miniphone jack, with a three-position gain switch: lo for line sources (tape, tuners, other Easels), mid for instrument pickups, hi for contact and high-impedance microphones. Reaches Gate 2 when SIGNAL ROUTING is up, the balanced modulator in 'balanced external' mode, and always the envelope detector.

modules.name: Envelope Detector
modules.description: Produces a control voltage proportional to the amplitude of the preamp signal, on the 'c.v. out' jack.

modules.name: Lopass Gate 1
modules.description: Vactrol lowpass gate fed by the complex oscillator (or, in AM, the balanced modulator). MODE SELECT makes it a voltage-controlled amplifier (no gain at 0, full at 10), a 12 dB/octave lowpass filter whose cut-off follows the LEVEL, or both at once ('combination'), where lowering the level dulls as it quietens. The lowpass element responds more slowly than the amplifier, which gives struck, resonant decays. Output to channel A of the output section.

modules.name: Lopass Gate 2
modules.description: Vactrol lowpass gate fed by the source chosen by SIGNAL ROUTING. MODE SELECT makes it a voltage-controlled amplifier (no gain at 0, full at 10), a 12 dB/octave lowpass filter whose cut-off follows the LEVEL, or both at once ('combination'), where lowering the level dulls as it quietens. The lowpass element responds more slowly than the amplifier, which gives struck, resonant decays. Output to channel B of the output section.

modules.name: Reverberation
modules.description: Spring reverb on the mixed signal, returned at REVERBERATION LEVEL.

properties.type_source: reissue documentation; the 1974 manual does not say

modules.name: Output Section
modules.description: Mixes Gate 1 (channel A) and Gate 2 (channel B), adds reverb, and drives the program outputs at OUTPUT LEVEL (nominally 1 V) and the headset output at MONITOR LEVEL, independently. Not controlled by the program card.

modules.name: Program Card interface
modules.description: The slot, the CONTROL selector and the card buses. The OFFSET line is a fixed reference that card resistors turn into offset levels. Two buses are reached through front-panel jacks: the card's INV column leaves on the inverter's 'from prog' jack, and the inverter's and envelope detector's 'to prog' jacks feed the card's INV and ENV DET rows. Jumpers between these jacks put the inverter, envelope detector, modulation oscillator or a preset voltage onto the card.

program_card.combine: Resistors in parallel sum their conductances. A resistor between a row and a column is both the connection and its processing level, so one input can take several sources, each scaled differently, which the front panel cannot do. With CONTROL at 'both', card and front-panel values add: offsets and processing levels sum, card and panel triggers both act, and switch codes sum too.
program_card.saturation: Inputs saturate above a total conductance of 10. Switch fields saturate above 6, so summed codes can select a mode in between: gate codes 3 (card) plus 3 (panel) give a combination mode the panel cannot reach.
program_card.note: Cards came blank with a supply of programming resistors; the manual describes bending, soldering and stacking them on copper strips. All slider calibrations line up across the panel so any setting can be read on the 0 to 10 scale.

example_patches.name: Pulser drives index and, inverted, modulation frequency (Patch-chart 13)

example_patches.name: Random pitch, timbre and level (Patch-chart 16)

example_patches.description: Keyboard-played complex oscillator, triangle mix, through Gate 1 in combination mode, shaped by a sustained envelope. The pitch offset resistor's value is not given.

example_patches.name: AM vibrato with pressure on frequency (Patch-chart 19, Figure 15)
example_patches.description: Adds to card_fig14: modulation oscillator in AM at 5 Hz and index .3, with key pressure raising the rate.

example_patches.name: Simulated echo with changing timbre (Figure 16)
example_patches.description: Gates in series; the self-running pulser (1 s) re-strikes Gate 2 and steps the sequencer, so each echo has a different timbre. Start with the pulser's 'one' position.

indicators.function: Inferred: a panel symbol beside MODE, presumably lit by the ramp or pulse.

behaviours.name: Offset plus processed control voltage
behaviours.rule: Every voltage-controlled parameter has two sliders. The right-hand offset sets the starting value; the left-hand processing slider scales whatever is patched to the black input below them, and the result adds upward from the offset. Processing at 0 removes the input entirely. To let a patched voltage define the whole range, set the offset to 0 and processing to 10.

behaviours.name: Three signal classes, separate connectors
behaviours.rule: Control voltages and pulses travel on banana cords; audio stays inside apart from the preamp input and the outputs, on miniphone jacks. Audio cannot be patched into a control input, except the modulation oscillator's 'mod c.v. out', which carries its waveform as a voltage. Banana plugs stack, so one output can feed several inputs.

behaviours.name: Jack colours
behaviours.rule: Black jacks are control inputs. Outputs are coded by source: orange envelope, yellow pulser, blue sequencer, white random, violet pressure.

behaviours.name: Lowpass gate modes
behaviours.rule: VCA mode: LEVEL is gain. Lowpass mode: LEVEL is a 12 dB/octave cut-off; with a 220 Hz square about 3 leaves a near sine, lower goes silent. Combination: both together, so quieter is also duller. The filter element lags the amplifier, so very short envelopes in combination mode give resonant, drum-like strikes. Response follows the illumination of the vactrol lamp.

behaviours.name: Gates in series, out of phase
behaviours.rule: With SIGNAL ROUTING at 'series', Gate 1 feeds Gate 2 and also channel A. The gates are 180 degrees out of phase, so mixing both cancels: Gate 1 as amplifier and Gate 2 as lowpass leaves a highpass-like sound, and moving Gate 2 between about 4 and 8 gives phasing. With channel A down, both gates must open for any sound: double enveloping and echoes.

behaviours.name: Harmonic addition
behaviours.rule: The WAVESHAPE knob crossfades a sine with the selected spike, square or triangle; it never changes the oscillator itself. TIMBRE adds and accentuates harmonics, the opposite of filtering, and acts only on the sine and triangle components. In the early 208 a second triangle oscillator tracks the first and is cross-modulated by it as timbre rises.

behaviours.name: Modulation modes
behaviours.rule: FM: index sets the deviation around the centre pitch; .2 is about a semitone at 440 Hz, and near 1.0 the centre is lost. AM: tremolo at low rates, sidebands at audio rates; above about .5 the fundamental fades and 1.0 is complete ring modulation. Balanced external: the same on the preamp signal. The modulator's waveshape determines the sideband density. FM index can also come from the complex oscillator's PITCH processing when 'mod c.v. out' is patched to PITCH, giving AM and FM at once.

behaviours.name: Envelope generator
behaviours.rule: Attack, then hold, then decay. Transient: hold is DURATION, independent of trigger length. Sustained: hold lasts as long as the trigger. With all three at minimum the envelope is under 1/100 s. The trapezoid can be inverted by the inverter or, for pitch, by the SIGN switch.

behaviours.name: Pulser and self-triggering
behaviours.rule: Each trigger starts a falling ramp; the trigger out comes at the end. In 'self' mode the end trigger restarts the ramp, but it needs a first trigger: flick MODE to 'one' and back. 'one' still works under card control. More voltage at the PERIOD input shortens the period.

behaviours.name: Sequencer
behaviours.rule: Advances one stage per trigger from keyboard or pulser; STAGES sets 3, 4 or 5, the card adds 2. Each stage sends a pulse unless its switch is down, to fire the envelope or pulser and so place rests. Patching the sequencer voltage into the self-running pulser's PERIOD makes rhythms, since each stage sets the next period. Tune each level using the keyboard as trigger source.

behaviours.name: Key voltages
behaviours.rule: 29 equal steps, held until the next key. Through a KEYBOARD switch they give equal-tempered half steps; through a PITCH or FREQUENCY input the processing slider sets the interval, from tiny divisions of a whole step to 2 1/3 octaves, for other tunings. Both oscillators on the same voltage track at a fixed ratio, so modulation timbres stay similar across the keyboard.

behaviours.name: Presets and shift
behaviours.rule: Three preset plates give independent voltages at the PRESET outputs. SHIFT 'octave' makes them select registers 12 keys apart (an octave only when the oscillator is tuned to 12-note steps); 'preset' adds the touched preset's level to the key voltage, for any transposition up to a major ninth; 'none' leaves the key voltage alone.

behaviours.name: Program card and front panel together
behaviours.rule: CONTROL selects card, panel or both. In 'both', offsets, processing levels and switch codes add, and card and panel triggers both act. Card routings can feed one input from several sources with separate levels, keep inputs below a total of 10, and expose card-only features: a two-stage sequence, sequencer pulses triggering the random source, and a voltage-controlled stage count. The fine tuning knobs, the pulser 'one' position and the whole output section stay under manual control.

behaviours.name: Inverter
behaviours.rule: Output is 10 minus input on the 0 to 10 scale. Its card jacks can be borrowed: a third random voltage can reach the card through the inverter's 'to prog' jack, and a fourth through the envelope detector's.

behaviours.name: Random voltages
behaviours.rule: Four uncorrelated levels, renewed on each trigger and held between. Processing near 1 gives slight variation around the offset; higher processing gives wider jumps.

midi.note: None. External control is by banana control voltages and pulses and the preamp input.

outputs.monitor: headset or low-level speaker, about 2 W

source_inconsistencies: The complex oscillator's panel range is 55 to 1760 Hz; Dave Brown measured 38 to 3500 Hz with the fine tuning centred.
The modulation oscillator's panel range is 0.16 to 50 Hz; Dave Brown measured 0.13 to 70 Hz.
The program card text gives the oscillator 'key' fields as 3 or 6 with hand corrections for both oscillators; the Figure 14 worked example uses 3 for the complex oscillator.
The card summary says the complex oscillator's waveshape switch codes spike, square and sine as 6, 3 and 0; the panel and pages 4 to 5 call the third position triangle.
The card text codes AM as 3, but the Figure 15 example programs 'a.m. oscillator' with no resistor, which would be FM.
Patch-chart 4 describes the vibrato as 1 1/2 times a second and also as repeating every 1 1/2 seconds.
The manual says the Easel comes with 10 program cards; Synth DB says six blank cards.
The manual counts 29 voltage keys; Synth DB says 32 keys, consistent with 29 plus the 3 preset plates.

modelling_gaps.detail: Modelled on the original 1973-74 Easel. The 2013 reissue and the 208C/Easel Command differ: MIDI, an aux input, extra audio and banana connections, a green modulation oscillator section, trimmable 1 V/octave scaling, card-bus inputs that add to banana inputs, and the iProgram and later card interfaces. None of this is modelled.
The lowpass gates' character comes from the lamp and photocell's slow, level-dependent decay. The manual gives only the qualitative difference between the filter and amplifier elements.
Known only as cross-modulated tracking triangle oscillators in the early 208. A model needs a measured transfer curve.
Conductance values are recorded as levels, not currents into a summing node; the saturation points (10 for inputs, 6 for switches) are as stated, not measured.
Counts for yellow, blue and violet jacks are inferred. A clear photograph of an original 208 panel would settle them.
